prompt: Implement percent-encoding and decoding by hand, working on UTF-8 bytes so multi-byte characters expand into several %XX groups. Complete encode and decode.
explanation: Percent-encoding is defined over BYTES, not characters, which is why you must call getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8) first -- an accented letter is two bytes and therefore two %XX groups. A byte is signed in Java, so masking with & 0xFF before shifting is what keeps the high nibble correct for bytes above 127. Decoding collects raw bytes into a ByteArrayOutputStream and only converts back to a String at the very end, because a half-decoded multi-byte sequence is not valid text on its own.
hints: Loop over text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8) and turn each byte into an int with raw & 0xFF before you test or format it.
For the hex digits, index into a "0123456789ABCDEF" string with b >> 4 and b & 0x0F -- that guarantees two uppercase digits without any formatting call.
Character.digit(c, 16) returns -1 for a non-hex character, which is an easy way to spot a bad escape; also check there are two characters left after the '%'.
